parts.title: ONE SEED — A WHOLE PERSON
parts.intro_html:
The descriptive power of the DAR system

A comparative analysis

chapters.title: Abstract
chapters.html: This study compares two ways of describing a personality: (1) the unified system of Fields and DARs and (2) a synthesis of six independent typologies — numerology, the Mayan calendar, the Zoroastrian totem, astrology, Human Design and Gene Keys. The comparison runs along five axes: combinatorial capacity, information density per unit of input, resolving power of the description (the spectrum of awareness), internal consistency, and dynamism (the ability to reflect changes in a life story). It is shown that the DAR system generates a space of distinguishable states exceeding the product of nine discrete typologies by roughly a factor of ten, while in coherence, testability and applicability it systematically surpasses the synthesis. Separately it is shown that the name-and-surname level (CHIA) is recomputed when a surname changes and can pass through up to nine states over a lifetime, which makes the description dynamic rather than static. The conclusions are supported by a computational experiment (200,000 calculations on synthetic data, with no personal records) and by a pair of portraits of one and the same person, annotated across nine semantic dimensions. The limitations of the method and the conditions under which the conclusion still holds are discussed.

chapters.title: 1. Introduction
chapters.html:
Most systems for describing a person — from the zodiac to Human Design — are built like reference books: an input feature (sign, number, type) is matched to a fixed description drawn from a finite dictionary. This approach is simple but limited: the resolving power of the system equals the number of cells in its dictionary, and combining several systems runs into their mutual contradictions.

The system of Fields and DARs is built differently — generatively. It does not select a ready-made description from a list; it computes the structure of the personality from the input data and generates meaning from the interaction of the fields. This study tests the hypothesis:

H. A single generative DAR system is able to give more coherent, testable and applicable information about a person than the sum of the known typologies.

Objectives: (1) to describe the mechanics of DARs formally; (2) to estimate and compare the combinatorial capacity of the systems; (3) to measure information density and resolving power; (4) on concrete material, to compare the actual coverage of the facets of personality; (5) to discuss the limitations.

chapters.title: 2. Materials and methods
chapters.html:
Material. Two sources. (1) Two independently constructed portraits of one and the same person — a portrait built with the DAR system and an integral portrait based on six typologies (no personal data is given). (2) A computational experiment: 200,000 calculations using the canonical DAR formulas on diverse sets of input data — to verify the real space of codes and the effect of a change of surname. Synthetic input data were used; no personal records were involved.

Capacity metrics. For each system the number of distinguishable states is estimated — the cardinality of the set of outcomes the system can tell apart. For discrete typologies this is the size of the dictionary; for multi-axis ones, the product of the independent axes.

Density metric. The information yield per unit of input: how many meaningful statements about a person are generated from a fixed set of input data.

Coverage metric. Both texts are annotated across nine semantic dimensions (cognition, emotion, closeness, shadow, growth, practices, awareness, time, mission); the relative density with which each dimension is worked out is counted by the frequency of profile-specific notions.

Caveat. The numerical estimates of capacity reflect an order of magnitude, not an exact "volume of the personality". Their purpose is to compare the systems with one another on a single scale, not to measure a human being.

chapters.title: 3. How the DAR system works
chapters.html:
The system operates with eight fields (LOGOS, NIMA, ANDRA, ZINGRA, LUBA, TUMA, ASTRA, BITRA) and generates a three-digit code Ma-Zhi-Kun, where Ma is potential (the feminine principle), Zhi is realization (the masculine principle), and Kun is their synthesis (creation). The canonical dictionary contains 64 named DARs; yet the mathematical space of Ma-Zhi-Kun codes is wider — the computational experiment confirms at least 81 distinct codes per level (for the TUNA level, about 90, because of its special Kun formula). Therefore 64 is a conservative lower bound on the capacity of a single level.

3.1. The four levels of calculation

A personality is described not by one code but by four layers of differing density of influence — from the dense core to the fine facet:

LevelInputInfluenceWhat it describes
ODAdate of birth100%the core, the backbone of the type
TUNAtime + Kun(ODA)70%manifestation in the moment, closeness
TRIAcoordinates of the place40%environment, the vector of growth
CHIAname and surname20%the fine facet

Each level is computed by the rule of repeated digit summation (reducing to 1–9) and yields its own DAR. Importantly, TUNA depends on ODA (it uses ODA's Kun), so the layers are linked rather than merely stacked side by side.

3.2. Generative, not a reference book

The key difference: meaning is not stored in a dictionary but is born from the interaction of fields within a code and across levels. The code 1-6-7 is not a cell "character No. 167" but the linkage LOGOS→TUMA→ASTRA, where the meaning of each field is modulated by its neighbours and by its position. That is why one and the same field sounds different in different codes. This moves the system from the class of reference books into the class of generative models.

3.3. The spectrum of awareness

Each field manifests not as a fixed trait but as a spectrum: a passive pole (energy freezes, turns inward), an active pole (energy spills outward), and a bright centre between them. The pole in which a field sounds is determined not by the position in the code but by the person's degree of awareness. Thus each element of the description carries not a single value but three states plus a rule of transition between them — this triples the resolving power of the system compared with a typology that gives one fixed trait.

3.4. The dynamic layer: name and surname

The CHIA level is computed from two inputs: Ma from the given name, Zhi from the surname, and Kun as their synthesis. Three of the four levels (ODA, TUNA, TRIA) are set at birth and unchanging, but CHIA is tied to the surname, and a surname can change during a lifetime — for example, upon marriage. This makes CHIA the only layer the system recomputes when a name or surname changes.

The consequence is fundamental: a person's profile is not a fixed point but can pass through several states of the upper layer. With a constant given name and a changing surname, Ma is fixed while Zhi runs through the values 1–9, and Kun changes along with it. This means that over a lifetime the upper facet of the DAR can take up to nine different forms, whereas the core (ODA) remains unchanged. None of the compared typologies has such a dynamic layer: the zodiac sign, the Human Design type, the totem and the Kin are fixed at birth forever.

chapters.title: 4. Results
chapters.html:
4.1. Combinatorial capacity

Below are the numbers of distinguishable states for the known discrete typologies. Each equals the size of its dictionary.

SystemAxisStates
Zodiac (sun sign)sign12
Chinese zodiacyear12
Life Path Numbernumber9
Zoroastrian totemtotem32
Tarot Arcanum (personality)arcanum22
Mayan calendarKin260
Human Designtype × profile5 × 12
Gene Keysone sphere64

If these axes are treated as independent, their joint distinguishability is the product: ≈ 9.1 × 1011 (about 911 billion) states. This is an upper, generous estimate of "all discrete systems together".

The DAR system gives 64 DARs at a single level, and a full profile has four levels: 64⁴ = 16,777,216 profiles. Taking the spectrum of awareness into account (3 states for each of the 12 field positions, 3¹² = 531,441), the total number of distinguishable states is ≈ 8.9 × 1012 (about 8.9 trillion).

IndicatorDiscrete systems (sum)The DAR system
Distinguishable states≈ 9.1 × 10¹¹≈ 8.9 × 10¹²
Ratio1×≈ 10× more

The estimate 64⁴ is doubly conservative. First, the real space of codes per level is not 64 but at least 81 (see 3.1), so the lower bound on profiles is 81⁴ ≈ 43 million. Second, on top of this static number comes the dynamic layer (3.4): the upper facet of CHIA can pass through up to nine states over a lifetime, so the system describes not a point but a biographical trajectory — a dimension that fixed typologies do not have at all.

An honest caveat: a full continuous natal chart in astrology has a very large space of states (on the order of 10²¹), which exceeds DARs in "raw" number. However, that space is interpretive, does not reduce to a reproducible calculation, and loses coherence when combined with other systems. Therefore what becomes decisive below is not raw numbers but density, resolution and consistency.

4.2. Information density per unit of input

The DAR system extracts from a compact input (date, time, place, name) four DARs, the participating fields, and for each field — a bright facet, two shadow ones and a practice for coming out. From four numbers a multilayered description unfolds. Discrete typologies, from the same input, give as a rule one label per system. The yield per bit of input data is an order of magnitude higher with DARs.

4.3. Resolving power: a spectrum instead of a label

Where a typology reports one trait ("you are a Virgo: criticality"), DARs report, for the same field: a bright centre, a passive pole, an active pole, and a rule of transition governed by awareness. A single dimension of the personality is described not by a point but by a segment, with an indication of how to move along it. This is a qualitatively different level of resolution and, importantly, of applicability: the description already contains a tool for working on oneself.

4.4. Actual coverage of the facets (empirical)

Annotating the two portraits across nine dimensions yields the following picture of the relative density of treatment (frequency of profile-specific notions in the text):

Facet of personalityDARsSynthesisCovered more fully by
Cognition, structure5017DARs
Emotion, feelings2825comparable
Closeness, boundaries4210DARs
Shadow, vulnerability3012DARs
Growth, transformation289DARs
Practices, tools224DARs
Awareness, choice264DARs
Time, rhythm, moment538DARs
Mission, calling87comparable

Across seven of the nine dimensions the DAR system gives a denser description; across two (emotion, mission) the systems are comparable. On no dimension does the synthesis surpass DARs. At the same time the DAR portrait (≈ 3,400 words) is twice the size of the integral one (≈ 1,650 words), with one source against six.

4.5. Internal consistency

A synthesis of six systems inevitably breeds contradictions: different traditions define the same qualities differently, and these must be reconciled by hand. The DAR system grows from a single root, so its conclusions are consistent by construction — no contradictions arise between the layers. Coherence here is not achieved by effort but guaranteed by design.

4.6. Empirical verification by calculation

To test the stated capacity not only analytically, a computational experiment was carried out: 200,000 calculations using the canonical formulas on diverse sets of input data (dates, times, coordinates, given names and surnames). No personal records were used — only synthetic inputs. Only the number of calculations and summary indicators are reported here.

Property testedExpectationFact
Number of codes at the ODA level≥ 6481
Number of codes at the TUNA level≥ 64≈ 90
Number of codes at the TRIA / CHIA level≥ 6481 / 81
Distinct full profiles (out of 200,000)almost all≈ 194,000
Distinct CHIA on change of surname (per name)up to 99.0 on average

The results of the experiment confirm three things. The space of codes per level is wider than the canonical 64 (at least 81), so the baseline estimates are conservative. Full profiles almost never coincide with one another even in a large sample — the space of states is genuinely large and well distributed, not degenerate. And finally, with a fixed given name, iterating over surnames yields on average exactly nine different CHIA DARs (all nine values of Zhi are attainable) — an empirical confirmation of the dynamic layer from 3.4: a change of surname moves the person into a different upper facet, and there can be up to nine such facets over a lifetime.

chapters.title: 5. Discussion
chapters.html:
The results support hypothesis H in its substantive formulation: a single system gives more coherent, testable and applicable information than the sum of the typologies. The argument rests on five independent points:

  • Capacity. The state space of DARs exceeds the aggregate of the discrete typologies by an order of magnitude.
  • Density. From a compact input a multilayered description is generated — the yield per bit of input is an order of magnitude higher.
  • Resolution. Each element is described by a spectrum (passive—bright—active) with a rule of transition, not by a single trait.
  • Coherence. A single root rules out the internal contradictions inevitable in a synthesis.
  • Dynamism. The CHIA layer is recomputed on a change of surname, so the system describes a biographical trajectory, not merely the point of birth — a dimension absent from all the compared typologies.

5.1. Limitations

  • Raw combinatorics. A continuous natal chart exceeds DARs in the number of states; the advantage of DARs lies not in raw volume but in the coherence, density and applicability of that volume.
  • A single case. The empirical part is built on one person (n = 1); this is an illustration, not statistical proof. A rigorous conclusion would require a sample of portraits and blind expert assessment.
  • The coverage metric. Frequency annotation is sensitive to the style of the author of the text; it measures the density of treatment of a theme, not its truth.
  • Synthetic inputs. The computational experiment was carried out on generated data sets, not on a sample of real people; it tests the combinatorics of the system but is not population statistics. Testing on a real base is the task of the next step.
  • Content validity. The study compares the descriptive capacity of the systems; it does not check the correspondence of the descriptions to reality — that is a separate task.

5.2. Indirect evidence of validity

The convergence of the conclusions of two independent systems deserves special attention. The DAR portrait and the synthesis of six traditions, having no common basis, converged at the core: the union of precision with a sense of time; the central tension "to join ↔ to divide"; the role of a conduit; maturity as holding both poles; strength from composure rather than from pressure. Such a convergence of independent methods is a classic sign that a real trait is being measured, not an artefact of the method.

chapters.title: 6. Conclusions
chapters.html:
• The DAR system is generative, not referential: it computes and constructs the description rather than selecting it from a dictionary.
  • In the number of distinguishable states it exceeds the aggregate of nine discrete typologies by about an order of magnitude; the computational experiment showed that the real space of codes is wider still (≥ 81 per level), and the baseline estimates are conservative.
  • It describes not a static point but a biographical trajectory: the name-and-surname layer (CHIA) is recomputed on a change of surname and can pass through up to nine states — a dynamic dimension inaccessible to fixed typologies.
  • In information density per unit of input and in resolving power (the spectrum of awareness) it surpasses them qualitatively.
  • In internal consistency it surpasses any synthesis by construction.
  • On the empirical material it is fuller across seven of the nine dimensions and yields on none.
  • The agreement of its conclusions with an independent synthesis serves as indirect evidence of validity.

Final conclusion. Within the criteria considered, a single DAR system gives more coherent, testable and applicable information about a person than the known typologies taken together. Rigorous verification on a sample remains a task for further research.

chapters.title: Quintessence
chapters.html:
The known typologies select a description from a dictionary; DARs generate it.

From four numbers a multilayered person unfolds — with light, shadow and a path to the light.

One coherent system turns out to be more capacious, denser and more applicable than the sum of scattered ones.
